learnerStatement: Simulated learner. This review finds problems; it is not evidence that anyone learned.
learnerBoundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparison of numbers and familiar household objects; no domain-specific theory assumed.

observations.prediction: Selected50% against33% and25% margin for50% markup; locked it in.
observations.exploration: Initial0% markup: price60,profit0,both percentages0. Preset50:price90,profit30,margin33.3%. Preset100:price120,profit60,margin50%. Preset200:price180,profit120,margin66.7%.
observations.reveal: Corrected33%; compared30/60 versus30/90,then60/120. Explained different bases and margin=markup/(1+markup),under100%; always name base.
observations.visual: Actual1257 ×936 dark screenshot inspected. Price bar partitions cost60 andprofit120 at200% with paired200%/66.7% counters. Full reveal legible.

prediction.reason: Clear choice tests confusing percent bases.

interaction.reason: Three markup values show same profit divided by changing bases.

payoff.reason: Uses actual money amounts to explain denominator change and limit.

clarity.reason: Labeled cost/profit bar and definitions make desktop task clear.

transfer.reason: Reusable name-the-base rule but no concrete new application.

playfulness.reason: Three presets allow reversible ratio contrasts.

complexity.conceptualDemand: Distinguish costbase fromwhole sellingprice andratio formula.

whyCool: A200% markup occupiesonlytwo-thirds ofthe sellingprice bar asprofit.
caveat: Fixedcost andnoothercosts;no tax,discount ornewproduct application tested.
effort: Approximately 3 minutes of actual browser review.
